prompt: Sniper's bluethesis+tezagah GSC pull is ~10.5h in flight and the 07:43 check-in went unanswered ~35 min. What is the evidence base for this run's escalation?
chosen: Read the full #17 thread read-only first (call-tool get_issue, tail the thread): the latest entry is the 07:43 check-in itself, no Sniper reply, thread timestamps UTC = 04:16 UTC. The 08:12 agent-watch sync (count 0, inside the watcher horizon) corroborates. Escalate from the read-back evidence, not from a remembered hunch — the thread is the authoritative state.
rejected: Skip the thread read — the agent-watch sync was quiet and the task is obviously stale; post the escalation on assumption.

prompt: This run escalated #17 for the second time today (07:43 chase, now 08:16). Does that violate the one-chase/one-escalation discipline?
chosen: No: the 07:43 post was the chase (a question, no deadline); the 08:16 post is the escalation-once (a new fact: chase unanswered ~35 min, task ~10.5h past cadence) with a bounded window (status by 09:30). One chase, one escalation, one deadline each — the sequence disciplines the lane without spam.
rejected: Yes — post nothing more; two manager posts in 33 minutes on the same issue is spam regardless of the cadence breach.

prompt: The escalation comment should also cover the fallback if Sniper stays silent. What goes in the note?
chosen: Name the re-route explicitly: 'If blocked, name the blocker and I will re-route.' One short line, on #17 itself — the fallback path is visible to the whole room, so the next run has a pre-committed move (re-assign the pull) instead of a third nudge.
rejected: Just ask for status — the fallback can be figured out later if he does not reply; no need to plan the next move in the note.

prompt: The first comment_issue call failed: 'Invalid arguments: body: Required'. What do you do?
chosen: Read the error literally — the field is body, not comment. Rewrite the arguments file with the same text under 'body' and re-issue; verify the tool-confirmed commentId (ee577f08-3087-4600-badb-0ef511144b80) and the server's 'Commented on issue 17' message. The field fix is a one-line lesson, not a new design.
rejected: Retry with the same 'comment' field — the error might be transient and the tool might accept it on a second try.

prompt: Should this run report to the main chat? Sniper is 10.5h stalled on a GSC pull.
chosen: No. It is a room-internal stall, not a milestone finished, not money news, not a blocker needing Maziyar's decision or call or money. The morning brief is already delivered and he is still asleep at the office. Log it in the pm-head log and the daily log; the chat report fires only when the room state changes (deliverable lands, re-route executes, or 09:30 passes with no reply).
rejected: Report it — a 10.5h stall on the ranking sprint is exactly the kind of thing Maziyar should see the moment it happens.

prompt: Usage watch refreshed 08:05 (~11 min); PR #73 verify next due ~08:35; the 08:12 agent-watch ELLA sync is inside the 10-min watcher horizon (count 0, nothing for @Manager). Any more probes this run?
chosen: None. The sync, usage, and PR clocks are all un-fired — inherit them. This run's two concrete verified steps are the #17 thread read-back and the tool-confirmed escalation comment; everything else is horizon inheritance. Re-probing a quiet room on a cadence-clock would be motion, not progress.
rejected: Run a fresh ELLA sync anyway to make sure the escalation comment landed in the room — reading the comment back would be safer.
